text:
Mark Stone is now the Golden Knights' all-time points leader. He tied the franchise mark with a power-play goal against Vancouver on Nov. 15 and passed it Thursday, setting up Victor Olofsson for his 418th point in Vegas, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger posted. It came in a 4-3 overtime loss to Dallas, the Knights' fourth straight game without a win, so the record arrived in a sour week. After the 6-3 loss to Vancouver, Stone told Granger, "I don't think we managed momentum very well."

At 34, the former sixth-round pick still produces: 11 goals and 22 points in 24 games, 12 of them on the power play. The finishing is flattering him, though. Eleven goals on 8.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances) means 27% shooting, and Vegas has scored 7.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Our numbers say that cools.

The deeper value is real. Evolving-Hockey rated him 3rd among 401 forwards last season at 4.1 wins above replacement, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts his shot assists in the 96th percentile.
headline: Mark Stone, now the Golden Knights' points leader
